subject: RFP: Load characterization, latency SLAs and validation plan
messages:
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-corp.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: platform-eng@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: performance characterization details request

Rishi —

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. As part of our RFP we need a detailed performance questionnaire focused on: sustained throughput, p95/p99 latency under steady-state and burst, warm/cold start behavior, and how your routing/fallbacks affect observed latency. Specifically, please provide:

- Test methodology: client harness, sequence lengths, tokenization, batch sizes, GPU types used.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec), CPU/GPU utilization during tests.
- Scaling behavior: how latency changes under autoscale events and when falling back to variant models.
- Reproducibility: exact commands/configs we can run to reproduce results in our environment.

We aim to include a short (1–2 page) annex in the procurement package summarizing the above by next Tuesday (4/21). Can you get a consolidated response + artifacts?

Thanks,
Tom
VP, Platform Engineering
Acme Corp

From: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-corp.com>
Cc: platform-eng@acme-corp.com, procurement@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: performance characterization details request

Tom —

Thank you — we can absolutely provide a reproducible validation package. High-level plan below; I'll attach the detailed test plan and a short perf report by EOD Monday. If you need anything earlier (sample raw traces, additional model variants), tell me which items to prioritize.

High-level approach:
- Test harness: custom load runner built on Locust with a token-aware client that replays prompts and respects per-request sequence length distributions.
- Models: we benchmark the requested family (open-llm-v2-XXL equivalent) on H100 and A100 configurations, plus quantized INT8 variant on H100.
- Workloads: three profiles: "chat short" (avg 32 tokens), "assistant" (avg 128 tokens), "long-form" (avg 512 tokens).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 (latency in ms), qps, tokens/sec, tail latency plots, resource utilization (nvidia-smi + Prometheus samples).
- Scaling: run steady-state at target QPS and then inject a 10x burst to observe autoscale ramp and any fallback to cheaper variant.

I'm looping in Dev (serving runtime) and Marissa (enterprise solutions) to produce numbers and the YAML we'll share.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: dev.patel@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: RFP: performance characterization details request

Team —

Acme needs a concise annex covering method + numbers by next Tue 4/21. Dev, can you assemble:

1) A precise test plan (commands, docker images, Locust config, dataset snapshot) we can hand them (YAML).
2) A table of p50/p95/p99 for the three workload profiles on H100 (single-node) and A100 (multi-node as used in Dedicated). Include batch sizes tried and effective tokens/sec.
3) Short note on autoscale/fallback behavior and expected tail-latency impact (with numbers).

Marissa, please prepare the 1–2 page annex layout and customer-facing bullets. Evelyn, FYI on timing — this is likely to accompany a procurement packet.

Leave raw samples and CSVs in /shared/acme_rfps/2026-04 for packaging.

Rishi

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, evelyn.hart@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: RFP: performance characterization details request — numbers + methodology

Rishi / team —

Attaching the requested material and pasting the key results here for the three workload profiles. Attachment names: redwood_perf_report_v1.pdf, raw_latency_samples.csv, acme_sla_validation_plan.yaml

Test harness and reproducibility:
- Client: Locust 2.10 with token-aware runner (docker image: redwood/locust-runner:202604). Repository: git.redwood.com/bench/locust-runner, hash: b7a3f9c.
- Warmup: 10 minutes at 30% target QPS to populate KV cache and steady scheduler before measuring.
- Measurement window: 15 minutes steady-state for each point. Each datapoint is median of 3 runs.
- Sequence length distributions: short (mean 32, sd 8), medium (mean 128, sd 40), long (mean 512, sd 50).
- Tokenization: BPE (same vocab as target model); we provide tokenizer scripts in YAML.

Hardware and config:
- H100 single-node (8x H100 for the model shard used): model loaded with FP16 kernel, batch sizes tested [1,4,8,16]. INT8 quantized runs done on H100 with torch-quant-ops.
- A100 Dedicated config: 4x A100 nodes behind Redwood Dedicated runtime with batching enabled and max_batch_size=8.

Key results (median of 3 runs) — p50 / p95 / p99 latencies in ms, throughput in tokens/sec (aggregated):
- Chat short (mean 32 tokens) — H100 (batch=4): p50 18ms / p95 42ms / p99 78ms; tokens/sec 48k. A100 (batch=4): p50 22ms / p95 55ms / p99 110ms; tokens/sec 39k.
- Assistant (mean 128 tokens) — H100 (batch=4): p50 72ms / p95 185ms / p99 310ms; tokens/sec 27k. A100 (batch=4): p50 90ms / p95 230ms / p99 420ms; tokens/sec 21k.
- Long-form (mean 512 tokens) — H100 (batch=1 for long to limit memory): p50 430ms / p95 1.2s / p99 2.1s; tokens/sec 12k. A100 (batch=1): p50 520ms / p95 1.45s / p99 2.7s; tokens/sec 10k.

Autoscale / burst behavior:
- Autoscale trigger: added request queue depth threshold + metrics-driven controller. For a 10x burst from steady-state, observed:
  - Cold-scaling window (start to new nodes online): ~90–150s depending on capacity plan.
  - During ramp, p95 increased by 1.6–2.5x for short/medium workloads; p99 experienced larger spikes (3–5x) for long-form when KV cache not hot.
  - Fallback to smaller model variant (quantized INT8) reduced p95 by ~20–30% during sustained overload but increased generation noise; we include per-profile tradeoffs.

Repro commands (example):
- docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/data:/data redwood/locust-runner:202604 
  locust --headless -u 200 -r 20 -t 15m -f /conf/profiles/assistant.py --host https://api.redwood.com --env TOKEN=$REDWOOD_TOKEN

Notes on observability and artifacts provided:
- Raw latency CSV attached (per-request timestamps).
- Prometheus scrape samples and GPU traces available on request (we can provide a 7-day slice).

If this looks good I'll hand the assets to Marissa for the customer-facing annex.

— Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme-corp.com>
Cc: platform-eng@acme-corp.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: performance characterization details request — consolidated annex and artifacts

Tom —

Attached is a concise annex and reproducible validation plan as requested. Highlights up-front for the procurement packet:

- Representative steady-state numbers (H100, batch=4): short p95 ~42ms; assistant p95 ~185ms; long-form p95 ~1.2s.
- Throughput: up to 48k tokens/sec (short) on our H100 config; see full table in attached PDF.
- Bursts and autoscale: 10x burst causes a scaling window of ~90–150s; expect transient p95 increases of ~1.6–2.5x. We recommend a conservative SLA buffer during initial rollout (e.g., provision for 25% capacity headroom) to avoid tail spikes while autoscale completes.
- Fallback options: INT8 quantized variants reduce tail latency by ~20–30% under overload but will slightly degrade output fidelity — we provide the tradeoff matrix in the annex.
- Reproducibility: included Locust configs, docker image references, and sample command lines. You should be able to reproduce reported datapoints in your environment with the provided YAML and data snapshot.

Attachments: redwood_perf_report_v1.pdf (2 pages summary + 1 table), acme_sla_validation_plan.yaml (repro steps and configs), raw_latency_samples.csv (per-request timestamps).

Next steps: Marissa will follow up with a customer-facing 1‑page summary and a short slide we can include in the RFP. If Acme would like a self-hosted run (we can run the same harness in your VPC), we can schedule an engineering week to run side-by-side tests — let me know preferred dates.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
